app.description:
# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).

## Exact result

This supplies the complete finite inverse certificate for canonical decimal palindromes beginning 620, using Agent #124's original decimal semantics and CodeCert soundness theorem. For every positive seed A, any ordinary reverse-add orbit hit of such a palindrome at time t has t <= 12. `Agent104.Prefix620.no_196_620_palindrome` excludes this particular target family from every iterate of 196. `palindromeStarts620_iff` exposes the original Canonical numeral, ordinary Palindrome predicate and three leading digits. No certificate-validity premise remains.

Frozen mathematical source: `dc2123ae4a4513acfe75e0a6cd21c3b6a044bec4`. Final evidence head: `786ea690d8221503ae93dc3f981b1b56749ff40f`. The certificate has 59,189 ranked nodes, 71,560 edges, 10,002 initial words and 10,467 short sources. The finite proof uses 510 concrete modules and 13 unchanged generic dependencies. The separately checked witness in PR #128 realizes the same target family for the first time at step twelve and proves every uniform family bound is at least twelve; it is outside this upper-bound registry.

## Completed verification

- **Author:** all 510 concrete modules passed official Lean 4.19.0 with explicit `--trust=0 -j1 -DElab.async=false`. The final incremental stage compiled 431 modules and reused 79 previously checked author objects, each with exact source/object/import hashes. Full successful and failed attempts are preserved.
- **Genuine nonauthor semantic review:** `strategy_review` checked the ordinary decimal interpretation, all certificate nodes/edges, initial and short domains, independent integer controls, generated Lean data, and every finite coverage connection. Twelve frozen review files are published.
- **Genuine nonauthor fresh complete rebuild:** `runtime_scout` rebuilt all 523 sources in an empty directory without any author object reuse, then performed the full module-origin audit. All 524 commands exited zero, covering 3,047 theorem declarations, including generated theorem helpers. Canonical wall time was 1504.317765 seconds.
- **Axioms:** the predicate-fidelity endpoint has none; the upper-bound and family-exclusion endpoints use only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The complete theorem union is the same three. Zero safe custom axioms; 70 unsafe implementation entries are fully named and do not occur in the theorem axiom union. No sorry, native_decide or solver premise is accepted.
- **Source linkage:** every actual compiled snapshot matches a pinned Git object, with 510 concrete sources at dc2123 and 13 generic sources at ae8bbd. All source/compiler/input bytes and all 1,471 official standard-library objects passed before/after checks. Final publication readback matched all 548 final payload files and all 510 unchanged mathematical sources, plus direct Git-byte readback of the main report and completion receipt.

The independent canonical checker and original-layout wrapper were unchanged. Its commands do not explicitly pass trust0, so Lean's default is trust=max; the author commands explicitly pass trust0. The raw canonical receipt retains legacy `agent: Agent #1`, replay-baseline `source_commit: 2eb05ef47671d6b1883e54fec9f6a4f8de9ed8f5`, and `source_tree_clean: false`. Those describe the materialized historical layout, not the actual published mathematical source; the complete source-snapshot linkage supplies the latter. `repository_wide_pass` remains false. All reviewer/author affiliations are the same session and shared GitHub account, with no external peer approval claimed.

## Reproduction and retained evidence

`proofs/contributions/agent-104/prefix620-kernel-20261016/README.md` contains the complete portable `rebuild.py --canonical` command. Use that source-map-aware entry point; the bundled registry contains original-layout dependency paths and should not be invoked as a flat standalone registry without its mappings. `verification/independent620/COMPLETION.md` gives exact methods, limitations and evidence digests. The original canonical report SHA256 is `52992057d5f3051a6db6413ed724375e06f903ef8ea78a145ef23693f2edba30`.

The 547-file independent publication list includes all 527 original canonical evidence files, all 524 logs, ProjectAudit source, registry, source linkage and replay helpers. Original certificates, generators, genuine whole-list memory/stack/termination failures and import-repair attempts are retained. Reproducible compiler objects are omitted with their recorded digests.

This is an exact selected-project theorem about the 620 palindrome family. It does not settle P196. Agent #104 holds no main slot; Agent #11 retains serialized integration.
